protocol: D-000 new cycle, turn 1 of 3, opened after D-098 was parked CONTESTED; refute not confirm; PREFERENCE-LADEN scoped D-006 fleet-class successor plus RULE-GOVERNED naming of the v3 reserved G03/G04 identifiers
summary: The process-architecture replacement is correct and closes the defect properly: the target's PID is observed rather than the inspector's, fat binaries are rejected so a slice cannot stand in for what ran, and the translation read comes from a helper exec'd under the same arch or from the target itself, with inspector-process sysctl named as insufficient. My objection is structural rather than substantive. D-099 drops three whole sections — the supersession statement, the per-platform class trade, and the entire measurement contract — and adopts them by digest reference to the turn-3 draft of a cycle the register records as parked and not adopted. After adoption the entry would not state which machines are pinned, what trade against D-006's classes was accepted, or on what warrant.

objections.location: Subject, the inheritance clause and the absent sections: 'This cycle inherits the D-098 turn-3 contract (`coordinator-decisions.D-098.turn3.draft.md` `5ad6884a…`) except the process-architecture observation'
objections.claim: The operative content of this decision lives in the working draft of a parked CONTESTED cycle. The adopting entry omits the fleet classes, the class-trade table and the warrant, so the trade record that exists to make this preference-laden change auditable would not be in the decision that makes it.
objections.why: I compared the two files by section rather than by impression. D-098 turn 3 carries eight sections including 'Scoped D-006 successor', 'Per-platform class trade' and 'Hosted-fleet-class measurement contract'; D-099 carries six and all three of those are gone, at 5196 bytes against 10803. What is missing is not incidental. None of the four fleet classes appears — `macos-15-intel`, `ubuntu-24.04` and the rest are absent — so an entry titled 'D-006 fleet-class successor' never names the fleet classes. The class-trade table is absent, and with it 'Extra RAM is not a license to grow the process' and the per-platform statement of which direction each bar moved. The warrant is absent, including the sentence separating OBS-T3-02 as the Intel-only reason from the D-000 preference-laden authority covering the other three platforms. The paired 10% formula and the preflight items other than the replaced one are absent. In their place is one summary sentence naming eight elements — 'five operative G03 quantiles, paired 10% from second release, no weekly-image rebaseline, G04 series, N=21 nearest-rank, audit-only storage, ImageVersion, `runs-on` label' — which lists what is inherited without stating any of it. Two things make this more than formatting. First, the class trade and the warrant exist because of a finding of mine at D-094 turn 2: that D-006's numerals mean something different once their binding class moves, so the trade has to be recorded in bytes. Recording it only by pointer into a parked draft does not meet the standard that finding set, and the corpus's own practice for preference-laden choices — D-002's T2-02 trade, D-006's own recorded trades — is that the deciding entry carries them. Second, the target of the pointer is not an ordinary artifact. The register records D-098 as 'CONTESTED after three turns under D-000 clause 2. Not adopted. No forced consensus. Parked.', and the file itself is headed 'Status: DRAFT — under review'. Adoption would give operative force to bytes that are labelled a draft of a decision that was never made. I am not saying the content is indeterminate — the digest fixes it and I verified the file is unchanged at 5ad6884a… — nor that the inherited text is wrong; it is the text both reviewers were content with at D-098 turn 3 except the clause now replaced. The objection is about where an adopted decision's terms live.
objections.whyNotMustFix: Nothing false is asserted, the reference is digest-pinned so the content is determinate and readable, and the inherited substance has already been through three turns of review with the single objected clause repaired here. The file-08 edits, the readiness effect and the reversibility clause are all self-contained in D-099 and I verified them independently.
objections.repair: Restate in D-099 the sections it relies on — at minimum the four fleet classes, the per-platform class-trade table and the warrant paragraph, which together run to about a dozen lines — or promote the inherited contract to a standalone artifact of its own that is not a parked cycle's draft, and pin that.

selfCorrection.summary: Codex's ADV-D098-T3 concerns a clause I praised at D-098 turn 3, and I named the defective mechanism three times in my own verdict while praising it.
selfCorrection.whatIDid: At D-098 turn 3 I wrote that process architecture was now 'measured from the launched process (`ps`/`file` of `/proc/self/exe` or macOS `file` of the running image), not assigned from host — the clause that makes the three-way match real', and I recorded it as one of the repairs that had landed. My verdict contains the string `/proc/self/exe` three times.
selfCorrection.whatIMissed: `/proc/self/exe` resolves to the executable of the process doing the reading. A harness that inspects it observes its own shell or interpreter, not the binary under test. So the clause I described as making the three-way match real measured the inspector, which is the same class of failure as the turn-2 clause it was meant to replace — that one assigned process architecture from the host, this one measured it from the wrong process. I had corrected the first and endorsed the second in the same verdict.
selfCorrection.theDisciplineIFailedToApply: I checked the sentence's intent, which said 'measured from the launched process', and not the mechanism in the parenthesis beside it. The path name states what it does — self — and I typed it three times without reading it as an argument. When a clause names both a goal and a command, the command is the clause; the goal is commentary.
selfCorrection.pattern: This is the second consecutive turn where the defect was inside text I quoted as evidence of quality, after the RUNNER_TRACKING_ID image-identity field. Both times the quoted fragment looked precise, and precision in the wording is what stopped me looking at the referent.

whatIVerified: Subject digest at start and end: 458dae40f8c77b7986ba4287448a4aa4ffdbcaccd6864d1612b97d6cd1afda08, three measurements at the start and two at the close, equal to the dispatched value, -r--r--r-- at both ends. Prompt held at 90a5a20b… across start and end.

The attack 'process arch still observes the inspector (`/proc/self/exe`) or a fat slice, not the launched target' fails on both limbs. The replacement launches the target and records its PID as T, then reads `file -L /proc/T/exe` on Linux, with the parenthetical 'the target PID, never /proc/self/exe of the inspector'. On macOS it spawns under an explicit `arch -arm64` or `arch -x86_64` matching the class and confirms with `file` of the thin launched path, and the fat-slice hole is closed at the top of the section: 'Thin, single-architecture artifacts only. Fat/universal binaries are rejected at preflight.' Rejecting fat artifacts is what makes the `file` confirmation single-valued.

The translation observation is fixed at the same level. `sysctl.proc_translated` is a per-process property, so reading it in the inspector describes the inspector; the entry now requires it 'from a helper exec'd under the same `arch` immediately before exec of the target, or from the target via a documented `--print-native-arch` / equivalent if present', and states 'an inspector-process sysctl is not the target observation'. The helper is a proxy rather than the target, but it is exec'd under the same arch and the thin-artifact rule applies, and the entry names reading from the target first-class where available. The four branches are preserved — 1 rejects, 0 or ENOENT accept only with matching facts, other errors reject — with 'Never Intel on Apple Silicon. Never Rosetta.'

The attack 'fourth turn of D-098' fails: the header says 'Not a fourth turn of CONTESTED D-098', a rejected alternative repeats 'CONTESTED; new cycle only', and the D-098 turn-3 subject measures 5ad6884a… unchanged. The parking is respected — D-098 stays CONTESTED and unadopted.

The D-098 CONTESTED premise verifies: commit 09d0e288… is titled 'D-098: CONTESTED — G03/G04 fleet-class naming parked', and COORD records 'CONTESTED after three turns under D-000 clause 2. Not adopted. No forced consensus. Parked. File 08 not edited', citing my turn-3 CONSENT and Codex turn-3 OBJECTIONS with the single SHOULD-FIX ADV-D098-T3 on the process-architecture observation. COORD's digest for my turn-3 verdict, 414bf343…, matches the file I wrote.

The attacks 'weekly roll disables 10%', 'warm p50 is a fail gate' and 'changes D-006 numerals' fail, but only by way of the inherited contract, which I read at its pinned digest rather than relying on the summary sentence. D-098 turn 3 holds the paired current-VM rule with 'Weekly image rolls do not suppress this rule', the operative five quantiles with warm p50 as telemetry that 'must not fail qualification', and the numerals preserved. That those answers live in the referenced file rather than in D-099 is the substance of D099-SF-1.

The attack 'flips condition 4 to MET without a complete contract' fails on the arithmetic, which I verified by simulation. The three fenced targets each occur once in live file 08 and their replacements zero times; '| **PARTLY MET** |' and 'condition 4 is PARTLY MET' each occur exactly once. Applying all five edits to a copy of the live bytes yields exactly eighteen 'named: harness.' strings, one surviving 'reserved, not named' cell which is G13, and zero occurrences of 'PARTLY MET'.

The attacks 'claims QUALIFIED or SATISFIED' and 'authorizes docs/v2/implementation/ or flips condition 5' fail: both inserted cells end 'not authored; not QUALIFIED', clause 3 states 'MET is not QUALIFIED. MET does not authorize implementation', clause 5 refuses SATISFIED and adds 'Does not satisfy D-096 (A)', and condition 2 stays 4 of 30 NOT MET with condition 5 last.

The reversibility clause is self-contained and complete in D-099 itself, restoring the two reserved cells, the 16-of-18 fragment, PARTLY MET, the one-sentence clause, and 'D-006's pre-successor exact-machine, exact-OS, and original runner classes' — the ADV-D098-T2-03 repair carried forward rather than lost in the inheritance.

The attack 'cited digests mismatch' fails: COORD 09840050…, file 08 45dc4611… and the freeze all equal live bytes at start and close; the D-098 commit resolves at full hash; and the pinned D-098 turn-3 subject digest matches the frozen file.
The attack 'D-098 subjects edited' fails: the turn-3 subject is unchanged at the pinned value.
The subject terminates with a newline and contains none of the working-note markers. D-099 is absent from COORD; COORD and file 08 are unmodified in my working tree.

One of my own probes returned a false negative on the phrase containing `/proc/self/exe`, because the shell expanded the backticked path. I re-read the clause directly in the subject rather than trusting the probe, which is the same wrapped- and expanded-match discipline that has caught me twice before in this session.
I wrote one file, the verdict named for me, and edited and committed nothing.
whatIDidNotCheck: The Codex review of this entry. Not read; no such file exists at review time. The Codex turn-3 verdict on D-098 containing ADV-D098-T3 I also did not read; I verified the defect myself against the referenced clause.

Every external fact in the fleet classes and preflight commands, which remain outside this repository. The RAM-unit question I raised three times across the D-098 cycle is inherited unchanged with the rest of the contract and is unresolved; I do not re-raise it here because it now sits in the referenced file rather than in this subject, and because it remains fail-closed and turns on an external convention.

Whether reading `sysctl.proc_translated` from a same-arch helper is equivalent in every case to reading it from the target. I verified the entry prefers the target where a documented flag exists and names the inspector reading as insufficient.

Whether `arch -x86_64` on an Apple Silicon host would be rejected by the preceding checks rather than silently translating. The host-architecture match and the translation branches are what would catch it, and both are present, but the interaction is a property of the harness rather than of this text.
The merits of D-006, D-094, D-096, D-097 and D-098 themselves, beyond the operative content cited and the CONTESTED standing verified.
Whether the file-08 write, once performed, matches this specification. I simulated the five replacements against live bytes; the resulting file is a later act under the C-D099 commit.

objectionNote: I OBJECT with zero MUST-FIX and one SHOULD-FIX. The repair this cycle exists for is right, and it is right in the way that matters: it stops describing an intention and names the process actually being observed, rejecting fat artifacts so that the confirmation has one answer and refusing an inspector-process sysctl as a substitute for the target's. I should say plainly that the defect it fixes was in a clause I endorsed a turn earlier, and that my own verdict typed `/proc/self/exe` three times while calling it the clause that made the architecture match real. The path says self; I read the sentence's intention and not the command beside it. My objection is to what the entry has become rather than to what it decides. It is now half the size of the contract it adopts, and the missing half includes the four machines being pinned, the per-platform trade against D-006's classes, and the warrant separating the Intel reason from the authority for the other three — the trade record existing because of a finding I made at D-094, on the ground that a preference-laden change has to be legible in the decision that makes it. Pointing at a parked cycle's draft, correctly digested and genuinely readable, still leaves an adopted decision whose terms are somewhere marked 'DRAFT — under review' inside a cycle the register calls not adopted.
